text:
Someone wants to know if the water is warm enough to swim.
Is the sea warm?
Water temperature?
How cold is it in the waves today?
Can I swim without a wetsuit?
My cousin is on the sofa at home and wants to know if the sea is nice for the kids.
I paid for two beach chairs, so tell me if it is worth getting in the water.
Would I be too cold if I jumped in now?
Could I ask you how warm the ocean is right now?
Should I bring a towel for a quick dip or a full swim?

Every cup of coffee or tea can be changed to fit the person drinking it. Most people have a usual order, but a temporary change is easy too. Someone tired might ask for a stronger coffee. Someone else says, make it sweeter, or, just one sugar please. A smoothie can be thicker with less ice or thinner with more milk. When a friend jokes that black coffee tastes burnt, everyone laughs, and then they ask for milk. Short words work best: stronger, weaker, sweeter, less sugar, no ice. A coffee machine or a drink app listens for these words and changes only that one cup. To keep a change, say keep it as my usual, and it stays like a note in your pocket.

Mr. Osei runs a small shop, and last month's electric bill was high. Between customers he typed on his phone: how much powr did the shop use today. The assistant understood that he wanted today's electricity use. It checked the meter and said the shop had used forty-two units since midnight, which was more than usual. Most of it came from the big freezer at the back. Mr. Osei remembered that a delivery truck had been loading all morning with the shop door open. He asked the assistant to filter the list so it showed only the freezer, and the assistant did. The line was shallow at night and tall in the afternoon. Then he said, remind me to check the door seal. The assistant set a reminder for six that evening.

When you order food from an app, you pick the dishes, check the address, and press a button. The restaurant gets a message and starts cooking. A courier takes the bag and carries it to your door, sometimes with one arm on the handlebars and the other holding the bag. The app shows how long the trip will take. People change a few things: the tip, the delivery time, and the notes for the kitchen. They might say, put a bigger tip, make it arrive by seven, or no onions please. If the food is late, you can ask where it is. A black bag keeps meals warm on the road. Most apps let you say these things in plain words, and the order changes before the kitchen starts.

Lena had just moved to the city and knew almost nobody. A neighbour invited her to a monthly game night, and her budget was small, so she wanted to bring the cards she already owned. In the lift she typed in a hurry: how do i shufle a deck for rummy. The assistant understood that she wanted two things: how to shuffle well and how to start a game of rummy. It explained that she should split the deck into two halves, let the corners fall together, and do it three times. Then it read out the rules in short steps: deal ten cards to each player, turn one card face up, and make sets. Lena practised in the lift until she reached the right floor.

Mrs. Patel was a retired teacher who still loved numbers. One afternoon she was making a big pot of soup for her club, and every ingredient was written for four people. She needed it for twenty-five. She asked the kitchen speaker, what is twenty-five times three. The assistant understood that she wanted two numbers multiplied, and it told her the answer was seventy-five. Mrs. Patel had guessed seventy, so she laughed and said she was close. Next she asked, what is half of seventy-five, and the assistant said thirty-seven and a half. She wrote both numbers on the back of an envelope and began to measure the carrots.

Walter was not good with technology, but his granddaughter had put a quiz app on his tablet. He wanted to play it on the train, where there is no signal, and he worried it would not work offline. He held the tablet and said slowly, can I play the quiz without the internet, and remind me tomorrow at seven to practise. The assistant understood both parts. It said the quiz worked offline once the questions were saved, and it saved the next episode of questions to the tablet. Then it set a reminder for tomorrow at seven in the morning. Walter smiled, put the tablet down, and went to brush his teeth, feeling that he could do this after all.

Dana was late for work, and the kitchen floor was a serious mess after breakfast. She grabbed her bag and said to her phone, start the robot vacuum for twenty-five minutes. The assistant understood that she wanted the vacuum to run in the kitchen and stop after that time. It sent the command to the robot, and a small light came on. The robot's camera looked around and found the table legs. It even went around a slice of toast on the floor, and then it told the phone it could not pick it up. Dana laughed, said thanks, and locked the door. When she came home, the floor was clean and the robot was back on its dock.

Nora came home after a long night shift at the hospital, still in her blue shirt. She was too tired to type, so she said to her phone, post the photo from the ward party and make it temporary, gone after twenty-four hours. The assistant understood that she wanted to share one photo as a story that disappears. It found the newest photo from the party, and the picture took a moment to load. Then it asked which friends should see it, and Nora said just close friends. The assistant posted it for close friends only and said it would vanish tomorrow morning. Nora smiled, set her phone on the table, and went to bed.

name: scale_recipe
does: A tool that changes the amounts in a recipe so it feeds more or fewer people.
inputs: the recipe, how many people it makes now, and how many people you want to feed
people say:
- Make this soup for eight instead of four.
- I only have a small home pan, so cut it in half.
- I have to crack six eggs for a big batch, so how much flour is that?
- Double the cake for my sister's party.
- Can you shrink these amounts for one person?
- My cookbook says six servings but we are two.

The router is the small box that brings the internet into your home. It sends wifi through the air so phones, laptops and televisions can connect without wires. Every network has a name and a password. When guests visit, they ask for the password and cheer when the video loads. If the connection is slow, people say, restart the router, or, move the box closer to the living room. Some routers have a guest network, so visitors can get online without seeing your other devices. People also change the password now and then, and the last time you did it, you probably wrote it down. A good router may cost about sixty dollars, and it can last for years.

Kai was running late for a weekend trip to the hills and had only a minute. He typed on his phone: whats the wether on the ridge sat morning. The assistant understood that he wanted the forecast for the ridge on Saturday morning. It said there would be light rain until ten, then clear skies, and the trail would be safe if he left after lunch. It added that more rain would touch the ridge by evening, so he should come down early. Kai asked it to make a packing list. The assistant wrote down a rain jacket, boots, water, a map, and a pen for his notebook. Kai grabbed his pack and ran out the door.

Ms. Green owned a shop that sold fresh peas and beans, and on Monday her laptop screen went black. She was worried. She said to the speaker beside it, I would be very grateful if you could help me, because my customers are waiting and I must print the order sheet from the main folder. The assistant understood that she needed the laptop to wake up and the order sheet opened. It said the battery was empty, so it asked her to plug in the cable. After a minute the screen lit up, and the assistant opened the main folder and found the order sheet. A fly landed on the keyboard, and Ms. Green waved it away and pressed print.

A game timer helps everyone play fairly. In a board game, each player may get a minute to think, and a message pops up or a bell rings when time is up. Timers are also used in word puzzles, where the time limit is narrow and the fun is in the rush. People change the timer all the time. They say, make it two minutes, or, give me thirty more seconds. If the game is paused, you can lift the lid of the box and count the pieces while the clock waits. Say start, pause, reset or stop, and the timer follows. A scoreboard works the same way: people say, give Sam two points, or, take one back.

Someone wants to know how far they walked today.
How far today?
how far did i walk todya
Distance so far?
I listened to a whole album while out, so how many miles was that?
Can you convert my steps into kilometres?
It was a difficult hill, so I want to see how much ground I covered.
What's my total for the walk?
Could you tell me how much distance I've done since breakfast?
Please tell me how far I went, because I want to know if I reached my goal.

Ana was hosting a game afternoon for her kids, and her hands were full of juice boxes. She said to the speaker, start a ten minute timer for the card game. The assistant understood and started a ten minute timer. Then Ana said, no wait, make it fifteen, the gray cards are harder. The assistant changed the timer to fifteen minutes and said the new time out loud. Ana also asked it to forward the game rules to her husband, because he was coming home early. The assistant sent the rules to him as a message. Her daughter put a paper flower on the table as the prize. The kids cheered, and the timer kept counting.

When you write on a phone or computer, there are small tools that help. Spelling checks underline words that look wrong. A word count tells you how long the text is, and some assignments have a maximum, like five hundred words. If you cannot type, you can talk and let the writing app listen. Some phones have a sensor that notices your voice, and if the microphone is muted, you can say, unmute the mic. People use easy words to change a draft: shorter, longer, fix the spelling, make it more polite. Editing means reading it again and changing a few lines. You can ask for a copy before you change anything, so the first draft is still there.

Watering is the most common job in a garden. Plants need water to grow, but not too much. A sprinkler can do it for you on a timer, so the water continues for ten minutes every morning. People change how long it runs and when it starts. They say, water the beans for longer, or, skip tomorrow, it's going to rain. Seeds are kept dry in a jar until spring. Soil should feel smooth and a little damp, not like mud. When the sun is strong, people water early or late in the day. A garden app can look at the weather and say when to start, stop or wait. You only have to tell it what you want in plain words.

Mr. Hall was a retired teacher with a new robot mower and a neat lawn. At breakfast he said to the speaker, mow the lawn at nine. The assistant understood and scheduled the mower for nine. A minute later Mr. Hall remembered his trip to the pharmacy. No, he said, make it ten, I'll be out at nine. The assistant moved the job to ten and told him the new time. He also asked it to skip the edges, because wet leaves had started to fall and could jam the blades. The assistant changed the plan so the mower would cut only the middle of the grass. Mr. Hall nodded, took his coat, and walked to the pharmacy.

name: share_photo_album
does: Sends a photo album to the people you choose.
inputs: the album name and who should get it
people say:
- Send my class trip pictures to Mum.
- I want everyone to know how the party went, so share those photos.
- Let Grandpa see the beach album.
- Mail the most recent pictures to my sister.
- Can the whole family look at the holiday photos?

name: check_front_door
does: Looks at the front door camera and tells you if someone is there or if the door is locked.
inputs: which door to check
people say:
- Is anyone at the door?
- I'm making noodles, can you see who rang the bell?
- Did I lock up?
- Let me talk to the person outside.
- Show me my favorite camera, the one by the porch.
- Is the back door closed?

Rosa worked as a gardener and had a bad cold. While her hands were in the soil, she said to her phone, remind me to take my medicine at eight. The assistant understood and made a reminder for eight. Rosa then said, no, nine, I want to eat first. The assistant changed the reminder to nine and said so. She also asked it to boost the volume of the alarm, because her daughter had borrowed the phone and turned the sound down. The assistant raised the volume. It added that the label said to take the pill with water and to rest for a few days. Rosa nodded and kept planting.

name: start_nap_timer
does: Starts a timer for the baby's nap and tells you when it is time to wake them.
inputs: how long the nap should be
people say:
- The baby just went down, tell me in an hour.
- I'm far away in the garden, so ring the remote speaker when the nap is over.
- She will fall asleep soon, so please start a nap clock.
- Wake me in forty minutes, I'll keep the house quiet.
- How long has he been sleeping?

Person: Can you start a workout for me?
Assistant: Sure. How many minutes do you have?
Person: Thirty minutes, please. I want to run by the lake.
Assistant: I can start a thirty minute run and keep the time.
Person: Actually, make it twenty. I have to pick up the kids at four.
Assistant: Okay, twenty minutes. Should I play your favourite playlist?
Person: Yes, and dim the lights in the hall first.
Assistant: I can't dim the lights, but I can start the playlist and the timer now.
Person: That's fine. Thanks.

Sam had just moved to the city and had never used a washing machine with so many buttons. His friends were coming for dinner, so he wanted his shirts ready. He said to his phone, how much soap for a small load, I think half of the usual. The assistant understood that he wanted the soap amount for a smaller wash. It said to use half of the cap and picked the cycle for his personal things, thirty minutes at a cool setting. Sam wanted to invite his neighbour too, so he asked the assistant to send a message. It sent the invitation. While the machine ran, he closed the window blind so the sun would not fade his colours.

Grandma June was not sure how to use her new phone, but she knew she wanted to call her son about his first salary. She said, call Peter. The phone rang and rang with no answer. She felt sad, so she asked, mark that call so I remember to try again, and remind me tomorrow at seven. The assistant understood that she wanted to be reminded. It put a mark on the missed call and set a reminder for tomorrow at seven. It also said she had a few messages in her voicemail and read the first one aloud. It was from Peter, saying he would call back soon. June smiled and put the phone on speaker for his call.

Mia, a student, was putting on her blue dress for a street meeting when she saw a lost cat poster on the lamp post. She said to her phone, find posts about the lost orange cat. The assistant understood that she wanted local notices about a missing pet. It found one from a neighbour and read it out. The cat's name was Peach, and the owner asked people to leave out water and feed her if she showed up. Mia asked the assistant to print twenty-five copies of the poster for the meeting. It sent the file to the library printer. She also asked for a daily alert about new posts. The assistant turned it on and said it would send one every morning.

name: group_speakers
does: Uses the sound engine to put several speakers together so they play the same music.
inputs: which speakers to join and how loud each one should be
people say:
- Play it in every room.
- I wonder if the kitchen and the hall can play together.
- Link all the speakers for the party.
- Keep the bedroom one low, but the rest louder.
- Stop playing in the garage.

Someone wants the speaker to play louder.
A bit louder please.
My hands are damp from washing up and I can't hear a word.
Do you know how to turn it up?
It's so quiet in here.
It's Saturday and the whole house is cleaning, so we need more music.
The kids are shouting and I can't hear the news.
Could you make it a little stronger, I'm over by the window?
Push it up a notch.
My grandfather can't hear the words, can you help?

Someone wants to know when the baby last ate.
Last feed?
When did she eat?
Show me the feeding log and unlock the baby app, it's easy to forget.
We flipped a coin to see who feeds him, so tell me when he last had milk.
Tell me when she last ate and when she is due next.
Was it two hours ago or three?
Could you check the time of the last bottle and remind me when the next one is due?
Please look it up because I lost count in the night.

Priya had worked all night as a nurse, and when she got home the morning was mild and bright. She wanted to move a little before bed. She said to her phone, give me an easy workout for twenty minutes. The assistant understood that she wanted a short, gentle plan. It listed slow stretches, three sets of squats, and some arm circles, with a rest between each set. It also set a timer. Priya asked it to remind her to fill her water bottle first, and the assistant made a note. A cool breeze came through the vent while she worked out. When the timer rang, she said thanks and the assistant marked the workout as done.

Someone wants two numbers added together.
what's 14 and 9?
Total of 14 and 9?
whats 14 plsu 9
If I have 14 sweets and my friend gives me 9 more, how many do I have?
I'm back from the shop with a mix of prices, 14 for the cake and 9 for the milk, so what do I owe?
Put 14 and 9 together.
How much is 14 added to 9 for the party tonight?
Could you work out the sum of fourteen and nine for me, since I need it for the bill?

Ben was seven and was going camping with his dad for the first time. He sat on the bed with his bag and said to the tablet, packing list. The assistant understood that a child needed a list of things to bring for a night in a tent. It read out a flashlight, a warm jumper, socks, a water bottle, and one article of clothing for rain. Ben said, tent help. The assistant created a short picture guide for putting up the tent, which was an automatic one that pops open. Ben clapped his hands and ticked each thing as his dad packed it.

Zoe, a teenager, was texting in the kitchen when her cousin from the US wrote that it was seventy degrees there. Zoe typed to the assistant: no idea if seventy is hot or cold. The assistant understood that she wanted the number in a way she could feel, so it said seventy degrees is about twenty-one in Celsius, which is warm but not hot. Zoe was going to visit next week and had to pack. She dropped an empty box in the recycling bin, put a light jacket on her daily list, and asked the assistant to save it. It added the jacket and two shirts to the packing note.

Tomas was a student who wanted to bake bread for the first time. At the market he bought flour and yeast, and at home he asked his phone, how long do I bake bread. The assistant understood that he meant a basic loaf. It said to let the dough rise for about an hour, then bake it for thirty minutes in a hot oven. It asked what size the loaf was, and Tomas said a small one, so it said twenty-five minutes. He set a timer. When it rang, the assistant told him to tap the bottom of the loaf: if it sounds hollow, it is cooked. Tomas tapped it, heard a hollow knock, and smiled.

A can of pens on a desk is a good start, but most writing today happens on screens. A draft is the first version of a text. It does not need to be perfect. After that you read it again and fix the spelling, change some words, and make it shorter or longer. A word count tells you how many words you have so far, which is useful when a teacher wants a certain length. When you have been typing for hours your eyes can feel sore, so people take breaks. A writing app can notify you when you reach your goal. Say, count my words, or, read it back to me, and the app will do it.

A post is a picture or a few words that you share with friends online. People can like it, which means they pressed a small button to show they enjoyed it, and they can follow you to see your next posts. Each time something happens, a notification may pop up. If the buzzing is too much, people say, keep notifications calm, or, only tell me about messages. A post that gets a lot of attention might double its likes in a day. When a quarter of your friends have liked a picture, you may feel proud. You can also say, hide this post, or, delete my last picture, and the app will do it.

An oven cooks food with heat, and you choose how hot it gets and for how long. The setting is a number, like one hundred and eighty degrees. A kettle boils water and clicks off by itself. A coffee machine can make a small or a large cup. People ask for changes in simple words: hotter, cooler, ten more minutes, or, keep it warm. A recipe is a document that tells you the exact time and heat, and you can ask the machine to calculate how long a bigger dish will take. A dishwasher has short and long cycles, so you can say, wash quickly, or, use the strong cycle, when the pots are dirty.

name: resume_audiobook
does: Opens the audiobook or podcast where you stopped and plays it at the speed you like.
inputs: the title and the speed, if you want one
people say:
- Where was I in my uncle's book?
- Keep going from last night.
- Play the heavy history book from where I stopped.
- Can you divide the long book by chapters and start at the next one?
- Slow it down, he talks too fast.

Leo was a teenager texting his friend in Sydney, and his room was dim because it was late. He typed to his phone: what time is it in sydney, is it more than ten hours ahead. The assistant understood that he wanted the time over there and the gap. It said it was nine in the morning in Sydney, which was ten hours ahead, so he could call after breakfast. Leo was drawing on his tablet, and he asked the assistant to lower the screen brightness. It did. Then he asked it to wake him half an hour earlier than usual, so he could call before school, and the assistant set the alarm.

Tia, a student, wanted to use the hot tub with her friends tomorrow, which was her favorite way to end a week. She typed in a hurry: will the hot tub be warm enogh for us. The assistant understood that she wanted to know the water temperature. It checked the sensor and said the water was thirty degrees, a bit cool. It offered to heat it, and Tia said yes, so the assistant turned on the heater and said it would be ready by tomorrow evening. Tia wanted to touch the water to check it herself, but the assistant said to wait for the green light on the cover. She smiled and went to find her swimsuit.

Person: I would be very grateful if you could help me. I have a long drive to the office tomorrow and I need to be sure the car is ready, so please check the tyre pressure.
Assistant: Of course. Which car do you mean, the blue one or the red one?
Person: The blue one. It's the one with the silly dent in the door and the new paint on the roof.
Assistant: Got it. The tyre pressure is thirty-two on all four tyres, which is normal.
Person: Great. Can you also fold the mirrors in? I parked in a narrow spot.
Assistant: I can't fold the mirrors, but I can tell you where the car is parked.
Person: That's fine, thanks.

name: heat_one_room
does: Warms one room to the temperature you choose and leaves the rest of the house alone.
inputs: which room and what temperature
people say:
- My toes are freezing in the study.
- I have a class online at seven, so warm the study first.
- I can't afford to heat the whole house, just do the kitchen.
- Get the bedroom nice and hot before bed.
- Set the lounge to twenty degrees.

When you buy something online, you get an order number and an invoice. The invoice lists what you paid for. A tracking page shows where the package is: packed, shipped, out for delivery. Many people think the parcel is lost when it is only late. Delivery times can change, so people ask, when will it come, or, can it come on Friday. If something is wrong, you can ask for a refund, and the money goes back to you in a few days. Most shops are happy to help, and a mild, polite note is usually enough. Say what is wrong, like, it arrived broken, or, it is the wrong size, and the shop will help.

Person: I would like to know what I spent last month, please. I run a small shop and my accountant is coming on Friday, so I need the number.
Assistant: Happy to help. Which account should I look at, the shop account or your own?
Person: The shop account. I used it to buy rope for the stall and a lot of other things, and I want to build a better budget.
Assistant: The shop account spent one thousand two hundred dollars last month.
Person: Good, we are still in the black this month. Can you move money to my savings?
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't move money between accounts, but I can remind you to do it at the bank.
Person: Please do, thanks.

Dee was a busy parent who had been up with the baby all night and felt tired. She spoke slowly to the speaker: I would be very thankful if you could tell me when the electricity bill is due, because I forgot last time and had to pay extra. The assistant understood that she wanted the due date for the electricity bill. It looked at her account and said the bill was due on the twelfth. Outside, thunder rolled and the lights flickered, so Dee asked it to load the payment page on the tablet. The assistant opened the page and waited. Then Dee asked it to remind her two days before, and the assistant set the reminder for the tenth.

Someone wants to know how many pages are left in the book.
Pages left?
How much of this book is still to read?
Are we nearly at the end?
I started this one in September, so how far to go?
I read every night and want to finish by Friday, so how much is left?
How many chapters do I have before the end?
Could you tell me how many pages remain, because I want to finish the book while I drink my tea?

name: rank_spending
does: Lists what you spent money on, from the biggest cost to the smallest.
inputs: the month and the kind of spending, if you want only one kind
people say:
- Where did my money go this month?
- After the wet week I had a huge repair bill, so show my biggest costs.
- Show my spending in order.
- Which direction is my food spending going, up or down?
- What do I spend the most on?

Mrs. Ford, a retired teacher, wanted to take her sister out to eat. She said to the speaker, book a table for two at Rosa's on Friday at seven. The assistant understood that she wanted a restaurant booking and made one. A moment later Mrs. Ford said, no, sorry, make it Saturday, my sister can't come on Friday. The assistant changed the booking to Saturday at seven and told her. She also asked if the place had good soup, and the assistant read out the menu. Mrs. Ford said she would love the mushroom soup. She set down her fork and her empty cup, and went to find her coat.

Someone wants the phone to read text aloud.
Read this to me.
Can you read the screen out loud?
Speak the words on the page.
I can't see the small print, so say it aloud.
Tell me what the note says.
I am slicing vegetables and my hands are wet, so please read my weekly grocery list aloud.
Please read the message to me, because my eyes are tired and I cannot see the screen well.
Could you read this article for me, since I left my glasses upstairs?
